pairs.subject: claimed-improvement-remeasurement
pairs.evidence: features/civicscore/scoreClaim.ts:2 The only 'claim' in this context is a citation ref for an MP's published contribution score (and duel.ts only compares two published composites), so nobody here claims that a code change made a pipeline faster or cheaper and there is no judge re-measuring before/after timing samples; a search of features/civicscore for watermark, ancestry, merge-base, workflow_run, inconclusive, is-ancestor, speedup and runner found nothing.

techniques.evidence: features/civicscore/scoreClaim.ts:76 The score claim is a deterministic recomputation labelled ungated. No claimant figure exists for a judge to wall off.

features/civicscore/duel.ts:24 The duel compares two already-published composite scores (tie/lead). It does not compare base and head timing samples, so the credited/not-earned/inconclusive verdict has nothing to apply to.
features/civicscore/duel.ts:12 No CI run series and no split by commit; these are display rules over graph values.
features/civicscore/scoreClaim.ts:21 The index is recomputed deterministically from psp.cz dumps. No measurement runs are triggered.
features/civicscore/scoreClaim.ts:60 No incremental run collection or cursor. The module takes the score exactly as the leaderboard carries it.
